candidateWorktreeProcedure.approvalBoundary: The operator must separately approve branch/worktree creation, staging, commit, tag, push, publish, install, and provider execution at the stage where each is needed.
assembly: Review the attributed dirty tree and select only intended full-source product/generated/test/docs/governance changes.
After approval, create codex/v1.3.0-rc.1 without resetting, cleaning, or rewriting the current user worktree.
Commit the reviewed candidate inputs only after explicit commit approval.
Create a new isolated detached worktree from that exact commit; do not copy the dirty directory and do not run git clean on it.
Require empty porcelain status including all untracked paths before generation, after generation is committed, before package build, and before freeze.
Build and verify in the isolated worktree. Freeze only the exact commit after every local gate passes and an immutable candidate descriptor is written outside the package tarball.
Any source, policy, package, generated output, suite, prompt, grader, runner, runtime, lock, or version change invalidates the candidate and its paid evidence.
candidateWorktreeProcedure.candidateWorktreeLocation: fresh private temporary or reviewed build root outside the repository and outside evidence directories

sourceBoundary.rule: A source candidate is reproducible only when clean commit identity and recomputed content provenance agree. A dirty-working-tree digest is diagnostic, never an RC identity.

currentDryRunBaseline.note: This is a dirty-tree 1.2.17 dry-run baseline, not an RC package or registry artifact.

candidatePackageProof: Build one actual npm tarball with lifecycle scripts disabled into a private temporary directory.
Record npm-reported name/version/file count plus tarball SHA-512 and byte size.
Extract into a second private directory and hash a sorted manifest of path, regular/symlink kind, normalized mode, byte size, and SHA-256 bytes.
Compare extracted imports, package pi entrypoints, bins, templates, profiles, schemas, benchmarks, and generated artifacts with the reviewed allowlist.
Install that exact tarball into a disposable home/project and run package, install, update, rollback, and doctor gates before any publish.

generatedArtifactPolicy.rule: Generators and reviewed sources are authoritative. Generated outputs are committed only after deterministic regeneration in the candidate worktree and byte-equality check; hand edits are rejected.

artifacts.verify: node scripts/capability-catalog.mjs doctor --profile .pi/piagent-profile.json --lock .pi/piagent-profile.lock.json --package-source ../ and require report.lock.current===true; process exit 0 alone is insufficient
artifacts.packageDisposition: source-candidate integrity artifact; excluded from npm tarball

artifacts.regenerate: after reviewed version/manifest edits, use npm package-lock generation with lifecycle scripts disabled inside the candidate worktree
artifacts.verify: npm ci --ignore-scripts followed by release identity and package tests
artifacts.networkRule: No network-dependent regeneration is part of FS0; the RC build records exact Node/npm versions and resolved lock bytes.

humanAndGenerated: README.md and allowed docs installation commands
annotated Git tag only after explicit approval
versionSurfaces.existingValidator: node scripts/verify-release-identity.mjs; at tag gate also pass --tag and --commit

currentDoctorState.candidateConsequence: The current root profile lock is historical/stale and cannot prove an RC closure. Regenerate only after the exact candidate source and version are assembled.

runtimeIntegrityClosure.authoritativeCandidateProof: The regenerated profile lock must include and hash every executable transitive production dependency reachable from the Pi extension, CLI, permission/MCP paths, and generated capability resolution; type-only erased imports are documented exceptions.
runtimeIntegrityClosure.candidateGate: A transitive production-import-graph test must prove every executable dependency is both shipped in the tarball and represented in the regenerated runtime integrity closure; package presence alone is insufficient.
runtimeIntegrityClosure.testOnlyBarrel: core-services.js must remain excluded from the tarball unless it becomes a real production dependency.

candidateDigestDesign.canonicalization: UTF-8 stable JSON with recursively sorted object keys; path arrays sorted by raw UTF-8 bytes; no timestamps or absolute paths in the digest preimage.
candidateDigestDesign.algorithm: SHA-256 over length-prefixed UTF-8 domain plus length-prefixed canonical descriptor bytes
candidateDigestDesign.selfReferenceRule: The descriptor does not include its own digest or storage path.
candidateDigestDesign.freezeRule: candidate_state becomes frozen only after a clean-worktree recomputation, actual tarball extraction proof, generated checks, integrity closure, exact policy manifest, local phase gate, and operator-approved immutable commit identity all agree.

rollbackBaseline.registryArtifactStatus: must be resolved and verified before RC cohort or rollback drill; tag/source identity does not prove registry bytes
rollbackMethod: Use an exact prior artifact/version, never git reset/checkout over user work.
Dry-run the helper, host, Pi package, project migration compatibility, and doctor plan.
Require explicit operator confirmation for the actual global install/rollback.
Preserve auth, settings, sessions, project profiles, memory, task evidence, and provenance; optional newer sidecars are ignored safely or handed off, never silently reinterpreted.
After rollback, run strict doctor and a disposable project smoke before declaring recovery.

candidateInvalidation.action: Mark candidate invalidated, preserve ledgers/reports, rebuild from the smallest local gate, and never resume or relabel paid evidence as comparable.

entryGates: All intended source is reviewed and committed with a clean status.
All generated artifacts are rebuilt and byte-current.
Every version surface agrees with the exact RC version and release identity validator.
Package dry-run and actual extracted tarball match the reviewed allowlist and contain no forbidden/private path.
Every executable production import is shipped and integrity-bound; capability doctor reports lock.current===true; core-services.js is excluded or production-bound by explicit decision.
Policy manifest exists, is task-pinnable, and its digest is in the candidate descriptor.
Local full verification, distribution, install/update/rollback, and supported-platform gates pass.
No provider or cohort run starts before freeze and separate approval.
